knowledge:
- key_parameters: data.mat=Normalized RNA-Seq gene expression matrix with genes as rows and samples as columns ;; class.vec=Character vector containing the classes of samples (columns) of data.mat in the same order ;; samples2compare=Optional character vector specifying which sample types to compare (defaults to all) ;; annotate=Optional boolean indicating whether to map gene IDs to gene symbols and Entrez IDs using biomaRt (defaults to FALSE) ;; gene.ids.type=Type of gene identifiers used in the matrix, supporting "ensembl", "refseq", or "ucsc" (defaults to "ensembl") ;; score.cutoff=Optional specificity score threshold in the interval [0,1] to filter markers, where lower scores indicate higher specificity and 1 means no filtering ;; directory=Path to save HTML output files when using getMarkerGenes.rnaseq.html (defaults to current working directory)
- alternatives: MGFM is the predecessor tool designed for microarray gene expression data, whereas MGFR is updated and optimized specifically for RNA-seq data.
- when_to_use: Use when you have normalized RNA-seq expression data with replicates across multiple sample types (e.g., tissues or cell types) and want to identify genes uniquely and highly expressed in a single sample type compared to all others.
- pitfalls: RNA-seq data must be normalized before analysis to eliminate systematic experimental biases ;; Replicates are required for each sample type to ensure precision, though unequal replicate numbers are tolerated ;; The algorithm only identifies positive markers (high expression in one tissue vs others) and disregards negative markers or multi-tissue markers ;; Setting annotate = TRUE requires an active internet connection to query biomaRt.

workflows.name: marker_detection_rnaseq
workflows.intent: Detect tissue- or cell-type-specific marker genes from normalized RNA-seq expression data and return them as an R list.
input: expression_matrix.tsv (Normalized RNA-seq expression matrix with genes as rows and samples as columns)
sample_classes.txt (A vector or column of sample class labels corresponding to the columns of the expression matrix)
workflows.stages:
1. Load the MGFR package and the normalized expression matrix.
2. Run marker gene detection and annotation using getMarkerGenes.rnaseq().
3. Retrieve and inspect the identified marker genes for specific sample types.
workflows.code:
library(MGFR)
data("ref.mat")
markers.list <- getMarkerGenes.rnaseq(ref.mat, class.vec = colnames(ref.mat),samples2compare="all", annotate=TRUE, gene.ids.type="ensembl", score.cutoff=1)
names(markers.list)
# show the first 20 markers of liver
markers.list[["liver_markers"]][1:20]
